newsitem.title: UK: Euro shares mixed, dollar slips pre-holiday.
newsitem.headline: Euro shares mixed, dollar slips pre-holiday.

text.p: Key European stock markets ended mixed on Thursday, with London and Paris closing well below their highs and Frankfurt dropping in late business as Wall Street slipped back.

The New York market was down around two-thirds of a percentage point on the Dow Jones industrial average as the last European market closed -- depressed along with bonds as trading thinned ahead of the Easter holiday.
New York traders said Wall Street grew nervous about a jump in U.S. long-term interest rates above the seven percent level.
U.S. February home sales figures were higher than forecast -- suggesting strength in the economy which could eventually prompt a further rise in interest rates.
On the currency market the dollar drifted lower, as thin pre-holiday trading exaggerated movements, but ended European business a little above its lows.
"There's actually not much trade going through in spite of the price moves. That didn't take more than just a few major sellers," said a currency trader at a German bank.
The London stock market, Europe's biggest, ended firm but short of the day's highs as the decline on Wall Street and weaker bond prices weighed in.
Traders had earlier reported pre-holiday caution amid uncertainty over higher interest rates and the British election campaign.
Shares were, however, underpinned by "bed and breakfast" tax-related trading near the end of the British fiscal year on April 5.
Bed and breakfast transactions, which involve selling shares and then immediately buying them back ahead of the end of the tax year, are used to book capital gains or losses for tax purposes.
Many market participants were absent ahead of the long Easter weekend break. The London market, like most in Europe, will be closed on Friday and Monday.
"Most dealing rooms aren't fully staffed. Some people have headed off early," one London trader said.
Market participants still at work were already fretting about the next tightening of American monetary policy after this week's quarter percentage point interest rate rise.
Analysts speculated that the Federal Reserve could boost U.S. rates again in May to keep a lid on inflation.
Pre-Easter caution and Wall Street's soggy performance also curbed the enthusiasm of the German share market, which fell back sharply in after-hours computerised dealings.
Interest in the car and financial sectors had earlier helped the blue-chip DAX index to a slightly higher close in floor trade in Frankfurt.
In Paris, too, weakness on Wall Street and in U.S. Treasuries trimmed gains on the bourse to around a third of a percentage point at the end.
Earlier, the French CAC blue-chip index had soared just over one percent, boosted by the expiry of March futures and options contracts.
For the dollar, meanwhile, concern over Japan's large trade surplus and disappointment that it failed to gain more after Tuesday's rate rise were depressants.

"The dollar had a good go at the upside this week as a lot of people bought dollars ahead of the Fed meeting and the rate hike. Then nothing much happened afterwards so it's coming off a bit," said one trader at a U.S. bank in London.
The U.S. currency slipped against the yen after concern expressed by U.S. Deputy Treasury Secretary Lawrence Summers about Japan's trade surplus with the United States.
"The dollar's slipped a bit on the Summers comment but it's very quiet in Europe with the holidays beckoning," said Tim Fox, treasury economist at Standard Chartered.
Summers said Washington had frequently expressed concern about the "dangerous possibility" that the Japanese current account surplus would expand substantially.
Treasury Secretary Robert Rubin will visit Japan on April 4 for talks in which the nagging trade tensions are expected to feature prominently.
CURRENCIES AT THE EUROPEAN CLOSE
The dollar was quoted around 1.6763 marks and 123.48 yen, compared with 1.6920 and 124.16 in late European trading on Wednesday.
STOCK MARKETS AT THE EUROPEAN CLOSE
LONDON - The FTSE-100 index closed up 11.4 points, or 0.27 percent, at 4,312.9.
PARIS - The CAC-40 index ended 7.95 points or 0.30 percent ahead at 2,656.68.
FRANKFURT - The 30-share DAX index ended floor trade up 10.93 points, or 0.32 percent, at 3,429.05 but the IBIS DAX slid to 3,407.83 in after-hours electronic trading.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold ended London trading around $348.55 an ounce after an afternoon fix of $348.15, compared with the previous London close of $348.75. Silver was two cents weaker at $5.13.
